title: Body & health
goal: Name parts of the body, say what hurts and how you feel, and understand a doctor's advice ('you should ...').
intro:
When you're unwell, Kannada again uses the **dative experiencer**: 'to me fever is' (ನನಗೆ ಜ್ವರ ಇದೆ) rather than 'I have a fever'. Pain is ನೋವು, and it glues onto body parts to make compounds: ತಲೆನೋವು 'headache', ಹೊಟ್ಟೆನೋವು 'stomach ache'.

You'll also learn **-ಬೇಕು** after a verb, meaning 'must / should', and its negative **-ಬಾರದು** 'must not'.

vocab.note: ತಲೆ ನೋಯುತ್ತಿದೆ / spoken ತಲೆ ನೋಯ್ತಿದೆ 'my head is aching'.
Also ಔಷಧ auṣadha; spoken ಮದ್ದು maddu in coastal/rural areas.

phrases.en: I've got a fever. (lit. fever has come to me)
I need to see a doctor.
Take the tablet three times a day.

grammar.title: 'I have a headache': the experiencer construction
grammar.body:
Physical and mental states are things that **happen to** you, so the person goes into the **dative** (-ಗೆ) and the illness or feeling is the subject:
• ನನಗೆ ಜ್ವರ ಇದೆ 'to me fever is' = I have a fever
• ನನಗೆ ನೆಗಡಿ ಆಗಿದೆ 'to me a cold has happened' = I've caught a cold
• ನನಗೆ ಸುಸ್ತಾಗಿದೆ 'to me tiredness has happened' = I'm tired

With a **body part** as subject, use ನೋಯು 'hurt' in the continuous: ತಲೆ ನೋಯ್ತಿದೆ 'head is hurting', or the compound noun + ಇದೆ: ಕಾಲುನೋವು ಇದೆ 'have leg pain'. The owner can be added in the genitive or dative: ನನ್ನ ಕಾಲು ನೋಯ್ತಿದೆ / ನನಗೆ ಕಾಲು ನೋಯ್ತಿದೆ.

**ಆಗು** *āgu* 'become, happen' is the key verb for changes of state: ಏನಾಯ್ತು? 'what happened?', ಗಾಯ ಆಯ್ತು 'got hurt', ಹುಷಾರಾಗಿದ್ದೀನಿ 'I've got better'.

examples.en: I hurt my hand. (lit. a wound happened to the hand)

grammar.title: 'Should / must': verb + -ಬೇಕು, and -ಬಾರದು 'must not'
grammar.body:
Add **-ಬೇಕು** to the **infinitive stem** of a verb (stem + -ಅ) to say 'must, have to, should': ಮಾಡು → ಮಾಡಬೇಕು 'must do', ಹೋಗು → ಹೋಗಬೇಕು 'must go', ತಿನ್ನು → ತಿನ್ನಬೇಕು, ಕುಡಿ → ಕುಡಿಯಬೇಕು, ಇರು → ಇರಬೇಕು. It doesn't change for person: ನಾನು / ನೀವು / ಅವರು ಹೋಗಬೇಕು.

The negatives:
• **-ಬಾರದು** *-bāradu* 'must not, shouldn't': ತಿನ್ನಬಾರದು 'mustn't eat'
• **-ಬೇಕಾಗಿಲ್ಲ** *-bēkāgilla* 'needn't': ಬರಬೇಕಾಗಿಲ್ಲ 'you needn't come'
• **-ಬೇಡ** (as a command) 'don't': ತಿನ್ನಬೇಡಿ 'don't eat (polite)'

'It's good to...' uses the verbal noun -ಉವುದು (spoken -ಓದು) + ಒಳ್ಳೆಯದು: ನೀರು ಕುಡಿಯುವುದು ಒಳ್ಳೆಯದು / ನೀರು ಕುಡಿಯೋದು ಒಳ್ಳೇದು 'drinking water is good'.

examples.en: You must drink lots of water.
You needn't go to the office tomorrow.
Sleeping well is good for you.

dialogue.title: At the clinic
dialogue.setting: Mark visits a neighbourhood doctor in Jayanagar.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.en: Come, sit down. What's the matter?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.en: I've had a fever for two days, doctor.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.en: Do you have a headache or a cough?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.en: I have a headache. My throat hurts too.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.native: ಬಾಯಿ ತೆಗೀರಿ... ಸರಿ, ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಇನ್ಫೆಕ್ಷನ್ ಇದೆ.
lines.roman: bāyi tegīri... sari, svalpa inphekṣan ide.
lines.en: Open your mouth... Okay, there's a slight infection.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.native: ಈ ಮಾತ್ರೆ ದಿನಕ್ಕೆ ಮೂರು ಸಲ ಊಟ ಆದಮೇಲೆ ತಗೊಳ್ಳಿ.
lines.roman: ī mātre dinakke mūru sala ūṭa ādamēle tagoḷḷi.
lines.en: Take this tablet three times a day after meals.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.native: ತಣ್ಣಗಿನದು, ಖಾರ ಬೇಡ. ಬಿಸಿ ನೀರು ಕುಡೀರಿ, ವಿಶ್ರಾಂತಿ ತಗೊಳ್ಳಿ.
lines.roman: taṇṇaginadu, khāra bēḍa. bisi nīru kuḍīri, vishrānti tagoḷḷi.
lines.en: Nothing cold or spicy. Drink hot water and rest.

culture: Home remedies are popular: ಕಷಾಯ (a hot decoction of pepper, ginger, coriander and tulsi) for colds, and ಅರಿಶಿನ (turmeric) in hot milk. Elders will advise avoiding 'cold' foods like curd and bananas during a cough. Pharmacies (ಮೆಡಿಕಲ್ ಶಾಪ್) are everywhere, and pharmacists often give advice for minor ailments.
